text.p: Mississippi's Legislature approved a compromise bill to eliminate the "marriage penalty" in state income tax rates, state officials said.
A spokesman for Gov. Kirk Fordice said he expected to get the bill Tuesday and would sign it by Monday.

The compromise bill passed overwhelminginly in the Senate on Monday and was approved unanimously in the House last week. It changes the exemption and deduction schedule over four years so that married couples would pay the same tax rate as two single people.

It raises the standard deduction for married couples to $4,600 from $3,400, and the personal exemption to $12,000 from $9,500. The deduction for single taxpayers would remain at $2,300 and the exemption at $6,000.
The changes will cost the state $10 million the first year and $50 million over four years. The compromise was worked out after earlier House and Senate versions differed on the phase-in schedule.
